angle: Treat AI like a shifting operating environment, not a one-off project—optimize for change velocity.
linkedinPost:
In enterprise AI, your roadmap now expires every 90 days.

MIT Sloan argues we’ve entered a phase where disruption doesn’t pause. From the field, I see the same: the model, vendor, or cost curve you planned around can flip mid-quarter.

The answer isn’t chasing every shiny thing. It’s designing for churn.

What works in practice:
- Modular bets: isolate use cases so you can swap models or vendors without ripping out workflows.
- A kill-switch culture: pre-agree criteria to shut down a path when cost, quality, or risk drifts.
- Budget the replatform: set aside 10–20% of AI spend for migrations and retraining—on purpose.
- Measure cycle time to impact and user adoption, not model benchmarks. If no one uses it, it’s not value.
- Vendor neutrality at the edges: standardize contracts, data schemas, and observability.

AI is becoming an operating environment, not a project. Build muscles for fast learning, graceful exits, and quick integrations.

How often do you revisit your AI portfolio—and what’s your pre-agreed trigger to kill or double down? #AITransformation #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
